The exec bodies come from VF_OP(sgnj,...,ah) in rv32Xfvec.hpp: vf##op##_r_##fmt##_exec replicates rs2, so GVSoC executes GNU-as vfsgnj.ah (001) as the .r form. LLVM follows GNU as, which is correct; the bug is GVSoC's.

non_blocking_notes_for_T3_T5: RISCVInstrInfoXpulpfloat.td VFCPKA_H_S_INX/VFCPKA_AH_S_INX comment 'the high lane of rd is kept' is wrong for RV32. GVSoC VF_CPK(a, h, 0, 16, ...) (rv32Xfvec.hpp:236-250, 322, 485) clears 2*width = 32 bits at index 0 and writes rs1 to lane 0 and rs2 to lane 1, so the whole 32-bit rd is overwritten. vfcpkb (index 32) only exists with FLEN 64. design.md line 202 has the same error. The $rd = $rd_wb tie is conservative, not wrong, for MC. T5 should drop it (GCC emits 'vfcpka.h.s a0,a0,a1' as a plain two-input build_vector) and fix the comment and the design text.
Packed rounding ops use frm: VF_OP_ROUND passes rm 7 = dynamic. None of the vf* records (not only vfcvt.x.h) has Uses = [FRM]. T5 should add it where GVSoC rounds dynamically.
GPRF16 has type list [f16] only. T3 needs bf16 on the GPR half class (or a separate class) before .ah patterns can be written with FPR16INX.
